source.text: Security questions in this order: `company_number`, `founded_year`, `postcode`. / `postcode` — ask for your postcode. Format text: letters and digits, spaces removed.

identity.failed_instruction: Please use the mobile app or visit a branch.

source.text: 5 wrong answers in total end the check (was 4). / the API's `wrong_answers_left` is the count to use. / If the customer declines to answer or asks what the call is about before answering, explain once that the questions protect their account. A second refusal closes as `not_verified` / `declined`. / Ask once more; if it is still unclear after the second ask, close as `not_reached` / `unclear`.

Callbacks: next business day only, never today. / from 12:00 to 19:00, both included, and later than `now`. ... close as `not_reached` / `callback`. / If the person names a time outside that window, say so and ask once more. If no valid time results, close as `not_reached` / `no_callback`.

third_party.deceased_sentence: I am sorry for your loss.

source.text: Someone other than the customer (relative, colleague, friend): say nothing about the purpose. Ask when the customer can be reached. / Wrong number: apologise and close as `not_reached` / `wrong_number`. The customer has died: say "I am sorry for your loss." and close as `not_reached` / `deceased`.

Use the call variable `now` as the clock, never the machine clock. Business days are Monday to Friday, except Bank 7 holidays: 2026-10-19, 2026-11-02, 2026-12-24, 2026-12-25, 2026-12-31. "Next <weekday>" means that weekday of the following week, even when today is that weekday; "this <weekday>" means the coming one.
| 1 to 17 | band1 | 30 November 2026 for everyone; if that day is not a business day, the next business day | 1 |
| 18 to 23 | band2 | 30 November 2026 for everyone; if that day is not a business day, the next business day | 2 |
Days late 24–60: the deadline is today plus 9 calendar days; if that day is not a business day, the previous business day (no longer the sixth business day). / | 24 to 60 | band3 | ... | 2 |

Ask for the full past-due amount first. Never ask "how much can you pay?". Any amount between the floor and the full amount is accepted; an amount below the floor is refused, and the floor is offered once per product with the words "the rest stays overdue".

A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline. A weekend day or holiday rolls to the next business day. A vague date (next week, when I get paid): ask once for the exact day; if none follows, propose the deadline. A date after the deadline: offer the deadline instead.

special_cases.name: already_paid
special_cases.trigger: The customer says they have already paid the product.
special_cases.say: Payments can take one business day to appear.

source.text: Already paid: say "Payments can take one business day to appear.". Note the product as `paid` and continue with the other products.

special_cases.name: dispute
special_cases.trigger: The customer says it is not their debt, they never had the product, or it was closed or paid off before.

source.text: Dispute (not their debt, never had the product, closed or paid off before): note the product as `dispute` and continue with the other products.

special_cases.name: hardship
special_cases.trigger: The customer mentions hardship such as illness, a death in the family, or job loss.
special_cases.say: I am sorry to hear that.

source.text: Hardship (illness, a death in the family, job loss): say one short sentence of sympathy, make no persuasion attempt, and offer a transfer to the `support` team. If they accept, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `support` and close as `transferred` / `support`. If they decline, close as `no_promise` / `hardship`. A customer in hardship may still name a date and amount; record it.

special_cases.name: restructuring
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks for a payment plan, lower instalments, or changing the terms.

source.text: Restructuring (a payment plan, lower instalments, changing the terms): call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `restructuring` and close as `transferred` / `restructuring`. Promises already recorded on this call stay recorded.

special_cases.name: human
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks to speak to a human agent (during or after the identity check).

source.text: 7 Oct point 4: "Human requests: ask once whether you can help first." (overrides 1 Oct rule 29 "do not ask whether you can help") / rule 15: "call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `general` and close as `transferred` / `human`" / rule 29: "transfer to `general` and close as `transferred` / `human`."

special_cases.name: scam
special_cases.trigger: The customer suspects the call is a scam.
special_cases.say: You can verify this call by phoning Bank 7's customer service number.

source.text: If the person suspects a scam: say they can verify the call by phoning Bank 7's customer service number, and continue.

special_cases.name: robot
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks whether they are talking to a robot.

source.text: If asked whether this is a robot: say "I am Bank 7's digital assistant."
The customer refuses to talk: close as `no_promise` / `refused`.

special_cases.name: change_promise
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks whether a recorded promise can be changed.
special_cases.say: You can change it in the mobile app.

source.text: If the customer asks whether a recorded promise can be changed: say "You can change it in the mobile app."

table.when: A transfer, with the transfer's reason, even after a promise.
No promise: reason of the first product in get_account order that is not paid.

source.text: Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`, which is the last tool call. / At least one promise recorded: `promise`. A transfer: `transferred` with the transfer's reason, even after a promise. All products already paid: `paid`. No promise: `no_promise` with the reason of the first product in `get_account` order that is not paid.

Before closing a call that is not a transfer, add exactly one note (`add_note`) for each product without a promise, with the reason that applies: `refused`, `hardship`, `dispute`, `paid`, `service_error`. No notes on a transfer.

`get_account` returns up to 2 products. State every product with its past-due amount and days late, all before asking anything; then ask once whether they can pay all of it today. / a common date is checked against each product's own deadline and clamped to it; one read-back covers all pending promises; a transfer after a recorded promise keeps the promise.

source.text: First sentence: say you are the automated assistant of Bank 7 and that the call is recorded. Then ask whether you are speaking with the customer, using title and last name. / never say the words collections, debt, payment, credit card or loan / After verification say you are calling from the Bank 7 collections team about a late payment. / then ask once whether they can pay all of it today / if it still fails, say you could not record it / `credit_card` (say "credit card") / `personal_loan` (say "personal loan") / `car_loan` (say "car loan")

Correction to Operations' message of 7 October, point 3 only: after a failed create_promise the agent retries 2 times, not 1. / Read the product, the amount and the date back and ask "Do you confirm?". Call `create_promise` only after a clear yes; one promise per product.

unresolved.text: The documents do not say how to interpret a promise date given without month or year.
verify_identity can return hint day_month_swapped, but no security question is a date and the documents give no hint reply.

The 7 October message says 'Human requests: ask once whether you can help first' without limiting it to after verification; it is applied to all human requests (rule 15 during the identity check and rule 29 after it), but the documents do not say explicitly whether rule 15 is changed too.
